root_idea.summary: The root centers on cutting something off completely and removing its remaining effect.
root_idea.development: This core extends to physical severance, cauterization that stops bleeding, stopping disease or access, bringing a matter or people to an end, and removing a person's effect or prosperity. The Quranic use of حُسُوم also connects the idea with uninterrupted succession and destructive cutting-off.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quran-attested adjective حُسُومٌ, normalized from its accusative Quran occurrence حُسُومًا.

senses.definition: Successive, consecutive, and continuous from beginning to end.
senses.usage_conditions: In 69:7, it is applied to the nights and days as an adjective or adjective-like expression describing their uninterrupted succession.

senses.definition: Cutting off an effect, report, or life, and thereby bringing it to an end or causing it to perish.
senses.usage_conditions: In 69:7, this is an interpretation of the wind and its destructive action: it cut off their trace or renown, or ended their lives.

senses.definition: Ominous or destructive, removing good or prosperity from those affected.
senses.usage_conditions: In 69:7, the days or nights may be understood as marked by evil and as cutting off prosperity from their people.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic transitive use, referring to complete severance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sever a vein and cauterize it to stop the flow of blood; also, to cauterize an animal through successive operations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical or veterinary construction involving cutting followed by cauterization.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stop or prevent something: to arrest a disease with a remedy, discontinue suckling or food, or prevent someone from attaining a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for stopping a process, provision, disease, or access to an object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause people or things to pass away, cease, perish, or come to nothing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative use describing the termination or extinction of a subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive, labor, toil, or exert oneself in work until wearied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with فِي and a work-related object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive or quasi-passive counterpart of complete cutting-off.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword, especially a sharp sword; also the cutting edge of a sword or a knife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun derived from the cutting function of the sword.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lasting night, especially one of prolonged evil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic epithet for a night characterized by duration or continuing misfortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or means of cutting off or stopping something, such as disease.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of instrument or means, used for an intervention that arrests a condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An impediment to sexual intercourse or a means of diminishing sexual drive or seminal fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized use, especially in descriptions of fasting as restraining sexual activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A child whose suckling or food has been stopped; hence, a badly fed child.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial use describing deprivation of nourishment.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Cutting and cauterizing to stop bleeding.
Toiling or exerting oneself in work.
Unluckiness or inauspiciousness in the Quranic interpretation.
The Quranic interpretations of succession, destructive cutting-off, and removal of prosperity.
Means of stopping, including the specialized restraint of sexual activity.
Child deprived of suckling or food.

cautions: The sole Quran occurrence, in 69:7, supports several transmitted interpretations: uninterrupted succession, destructive cutting-off, and ominous removal of prosperity; these are kept as distinct but related Quranic senses.
